# Trellis AI guide

Last verified against Trellis main (2026-08-29).

Canonical full guide:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qlever-llc/trellis/main/docs/static/llms-full.txt

Use this file when generating code for a Trellis service repository or browser
app repository. Prefer the full guide when you need examples, contract workflow,
prepared events, browser-app wiring, generated SDK notes, or verification
commands.

## Current model

- Consumer projects manage local or OCI canonical API dependencies with `trellis add`,
  `trellis rm`, `trellis update`, and lock-stable `trellis install`. Commit
  `trellis.toml` and `trellis.lock`; ignore `.trellis/`. Remote locks include an
  exact OCI manifest digest and reuse Docker credentials. Install verifies API
  ID, release, semantic and OCI digests, generates SDKs before participant source
  evaluation, and never executes provider source. TypeScript links the local
  `@trellis/apis` aggregate; Rust path-depends on `trellis-apis`.
- The Rust platform runtime is the sole auth owner. TypeScript owns portal source,
  generated SDKs, clients, proof bindings, and tests, but no auth runtime state.
- HTTP is limited to browser/account flows, initial service/device bootstrap,
  proof-bound recovery, and portal assets. Connected control uses
  generated RPC, operation, and event APIs over NATS; there is no HTTP context
  registry, revocation, logout, or client-bootstrap API.
- Runtime boundaries use `trellis.api.v1` and `trellis.participant.v1` artifacts.
  TypeScript contracts are compiled to those artifacts before bootstrap.
- Contract authoring supplies participant identity, owned API identity, and API
  release version independently. TypeScript `define*Contract` bodies require
  `id`, `apiId`, and Semantic Version `apiVersion`. Rust
  `ContractBuilder::authoring(participant_id, api_id, api_version, ...)` requires
  the same values explicitly. API release version is metadata and does not enter
  API digests, participant evidence, permissions, or transport subjects.
- Large Rust store and transfer bodies use borrowed Tokio readers and writers;
  whole-buffer helpers remain conveniences. Transfer completion and cancellation
  are authenticated and acknowledged, with completion bound to exact size and
  SHA-256 digest. Transfer grants cap frames at 1 MiB.
- Bootstrap returns a deny-all JWT plus a root-pinned, issuer-signed short-lived
  authorization context. Every NATS connect and reconnect uses the standard NATS
  nonce signature and a digest-only context-selection token; there is no shared
  sentinel credential or second Trellis handshake proof.
- Ordinary context expiry still permits delayed historical event verification;
  explicit context revocation invalidates every RPC and event proof from that
  context, including proofs created before revocation.
- Trellis runtime authority comes from deployment authority and identity
  authority.
- The trust chain is a pinned root, a root-signed current manifest containing
  active issuer public keys, and an issuer-signed short-lived context. Clients
  durably pin root and API digests, verify TypeScript consumers through the
  Rust/WASM verifier, persist an observed `manifest.current` advance before
  invalidating and refreshing their own context, and compute deterministic
  digest-jittered refresh time.
  Clearing a session retains the trust floor. Bootstrap supplies the complete
  current trust chain; connected trust lookup uses NATS KV, not HTTP.
  Connected providers use a private digest-keyed cache over the internal NATS KV
  authorization registry, not HTTP. They watch manifest generation and
  revocations, become ready after current manifest verification and revocation
  state, and retain each verified context as an opaque Rust/WASM handle for
  repeated request/event proofs. Manifest changes discard those handles, and
  providers fail closed only on actual connection/watch failure.
  Registry handles are not service-author APIs.
  Ordinary request and event proof v1 verification is local,
  exact-permission/capability checked, and performs no Auth RPC,
  HTTP, SQLite, or registry read on a cache hit.
- The deny-all bootstrap JWT only selects the Auth Callout route. Context refresh
  is restart recovery, atomically renews it with the verified context, and
  returns route/session/NATS metadata plus its exact expiry. Clients retain the
  session/trust floor and send `currentContextDigest: null` for proof-bound
  recovery after context or route-JWT expiry. Pending devices retry
  `/bootstrap/device` with fresh request proofs; there is no separate activation
  wait or connect-info route.
- Bootstrap and refresh return server time in milliseconds. Clients use a request
  midpoint offset for validity and refresh scheduling; same-digest refresh success
  still reschedules. `maximumContextBytes` means canonical complete signed-context
  JSON UTF-8 bytes, not base64url token length.
- Signed authorization integers use the JSON safe-integer range, and context
  decisions recheck the current minimum accepted manifest generation.
- Deployment authority proposal/desired `needs` are grouped by `contracts`,
  `surfaces`, `capabilities`, and `resources`. Materialized authority is a
  projection; runtime `grants` are grouped by `capabilities`, `surfaces`, and
  `nats`, and permissions require current materialization for the accepted
  desired authority version. Stale or obsolete persisted projections are repaired
  by Trellis storage upgrade and reconciliation.
- Deployment materialization is shared by the deployment and exact participant.
  Session, instance, device, and delegation eligibility is checked separately;
  one unhealthy instance does not rewrite authority for healthy peers.
- Pure participant resolution pins every referenced API by exact ID and digest,
  keeps required and optional grants separate, and derives alias-independent
  machine needs. Named capabilities identify their exact defining API digest and
  explain fully selected exact permissions; they never add permissions to a
  participant request.
- Service/device bootstrap presents canonical participant and referenced API
  artifacts. Trellis classifies additive compatible changes as updates and
  incompatible API changes as migrations; both require an immutable authority
  decision. Each deployment + participant has one stable authority lineage.
  Equivalent pending retries reuse one proposal; terminal history remains
  queryable and never blocks later reproposal.
- Service bootstrap polls pending deployment authority until it becomes ready by
  default. Rust callers may set an explicit overall authority-pending timeout;
  request timeouts remain bounded.
- The runtime `contracts` store is a manifest cache keyed by digest, not durable
  authority. If Trellis asks for a missing manifest or prunes an invalid cached
  manifest, present the canonical participant/API artifacts again instead of editing runtime
  authority or implementation-offer records.
- Physical resource bindings never grant access. Exact resource permission atoms
  must be in `GrantSet`, and optional evidence contributes only optional atoms.
- Browser approval submits only the server consent digest, selected server-issued
  optional bundle ids, decision, and idempotency key. OIDC callbacks require the
  state-specific browser cookie and current portal policy. Consent is immutable
  for the lifetime of the browser flow.
- Trusted portal policy is exact to portal + participant. Base capabilities and
  groups plus verified provider-role mappings may select only capabilities in
  the server-owned proposal. Successful trusted local registration applies the
  same policy immediately as local or OIDC login. Policy changes reconcile
  existing portal-managed identity authority and revoke superseded contexts;
  removing the portal, provider allowance, or policy also clears verified-role
  provenance. Restoring configuration alone cannot resurrect authority; a new
  verified login must supply fresh roles. Retained sessions remain available for
  compliant clients to refresh and reconnect after eligible authority returns.
- Bootstrap replay revalidates current authority and mints a fresh credential;
  public errors never expose internal storage, crypto, provider, or topology causes.
- Device activation uses repeated fresh proof-bound `POST /bootstrap/device`
  requests. `Auth.DeviceUserAuthorities.Resolve` claims the durable expiring
  review for one user; administrative approval cannot complete missing required
  delegation, server-side operation wait is event-driven, and cancellation is
  unsupported.
- Caller-visible communication is contract-driven and runs through generated
  RPC, event, feed, and operation surfaces. Resources, state, files, and jobs are
  contract-declared runtime surfaces; jobs are service-private background work.
- Browser apps that already hold record references to Trellis user ids can
  declare `Auth.Users.Resolve` to render minimal labels. Do not use
  `Auth.Users.List` or invent app-local user tables for basic display labels.
- Normal TypeScript contract authoring imports `define*Contract(...)` helpers from
  the browser-safe `@qlever-llc/trellis` root. Runtime-specific helpers,
  generated SDKs, browser auth, device activation, telemetry, and advanced
  contract tooling stay on explicit subpaths.
- Trellis public API object schemas are open by default. For contract schemas
  used by public RPC input/output, events, operation input/progress/output, feeds,
  or exported generated schemas, omit `additionalProperties` in every authoring
  language unless a security-sensitive proof boundary or another documented
  requirement must reject unknown fields. Ignoring unknown fields keeps older
  clients and newer servers forward-compatible.
- Durable event processing uses contract-declared `eventConsumers` resources;
  `eventConsumers.<group>.uses` selects dependency events by top-level `uses`
  alias, and `eventConsumers.<group>.self` selects events owned by the same
  contract. Dependency durable consumption remains authority-backed by top-level
  `uses`; runtime durable consumers are Trellis-provisioned only.
- Rust durable event listeners use generated group handlers from
  `service.event_consumers()` and must not provide caller-owned durable names. The
  returned handle supports `abort()`; aborting a durable listener removes that
  handler registration so re-registering can resume delivery from the same
  Trellis-provisioned durable consumer.
- Trellis does not provide application dependency injection. Handler arguments
  contain only Trellis-owned runtime data. Application resources are supplied by
  normal JavaScript closure or factory patterns.
- Trellis libraries do not expose raw NATS connection handles as application API.
  Use generated surfaces, service resource handles, and `TrellisConnection` for
  lifecycle status and shutdown.
- Use operations for caller-visible async workflows. Use jobs for service-private
  background execution. Both remain inside transport permissions compiled from
  the connected principal's current authorization context; subject names and
  operation/job declarations never create grants.
- Rust low-level Jobs lifecycle constructors are module-scoped under
  `trellis_rs::jobs::events` and take `events::EventMeta` for common metadata.
  Current-attempt constructors take `tries` separately; zero-attempt
  constructors do not. Do not import constructors from `trellis_rs::jobs`.
- Operations and job queues may declare one optional `update` schema. Keep
  `progress` for low-frequency durable telemetry/snapshots; updates are typed
  live-only, at-most-once content with no persistence, replay, admin, or Event
  Log surface. Watchers must opt in, late subscribers may miss frames, cumulative
  payloads are preferred, and terminal output/result is authoritative.
- Active jobs emit updates and `JobRef` or queue-by-job-id subscriptions consume
  them. Job update subscriptions filter stale attempts and duplicate or
  out-of-order attempt-local sequences and must be cleaned up. SQL-outbox callers
  subscribe using the preallocated `jobId` before dispatch when early frames
  matter. Job update subjects are private Core NATS outside `JOBS`.
- Jobs admin is a clean-break workbench surface: use `Jobs.Query` for server-side
  search/sort/group/stats, `Jobs.Metrics` for grouped operational summaries and
  time buckets, and `Jobs.Inspect` for one-job detail, timeline, attempts,
  related jobs, errors, trigger, lineage, and current `waitingOn` edges. Jobs
  remain `active` while waiting; use active-job wait helpers to annotate long
  external async work. Do not use removed `Jobs.List` or `Jobs.Get`; `Jobs.Watch`
  only emits invalidations, so rerun the query,
  metrics, or inspection read.
- Event Log admin is read-only: use `EventLog.Query`, `EventLog.Inspect`,
  `EventLog.Metrics`, `EventLog.Consumers.Query`, and `EventLog.Watch` for event
  observability. Declare it as an optional dependency unless the app cannot
  operate without historical event data. Publisher deployment attribution comes
  from verified event session proof, while owner contract/event comes from
  subject/catalog matching. `EventLog.Query` accepts `includeEventTypes` and
  `excludeEventTypes` arrays of owner contract/event pairs and
  `integrityExceptionOnly` for events whose owner resolution or proof verification
  failed. `EventLog.Metrics` returns exact `summary.integrityExceptions`, resolved
  event-type counts, and typed time buckets with volume, payload size, resolution,
  and verification counts.
- For service-private work that must be singleton per logical entity, declare
  job `keyConcurrency` instead of building ad hoc scheduler dedupe. Defaults
  should fail clearly (`stalePolicy: "fail-stale"`, `whenFull: "reject"`);
  coalescing or replacing queued work must be explicit. Configure worker counts
  in each service implementation, never in the contract or resource binding.
- TypeScript job handlers that need JetStream redelivery should return or throw
  `RetryJobError` from `@qlever-llc/trellis/jobs`; ordinary errors remain
  terminal job failures.
- Rust active jobs use JetStream-derived attempt/redelivery metadata. Retryable
  failures NAK before the final allowed delivery; the final delivery remains
  unacknowledged so `AckWait` drives the durable MaxDeliver advisory.
- Jobs admin mutations accept optional `reason`; active cancellation is
  cooperative through `Jobs.Cancel`. Do not invent hard stop/kill APIs. The
  SQLite jobs projection is disposable; the `JOBS` stream remains the source of
  truth.
- Operations support declared typed errors, following the same error-declaration
  rules as RPC errors on the operation descriptor.
- Model expected public failures with declared errors or `Result`-style values.
- TypeScript services use `service.createSqlOutbox(...)` for SQL transactional
  event enqueue and job submission. Close over the outbox object as a plain dependency, use
  `outbox.transaction(...)` around all DB work and `event.*.*.enqueue(...)` or
  `job.*.*.create/submit(...)` calls that must commit atomically, and do not create local outbox wrappers or manual
  `SqlOutboxRepository` handler wiring. Normal event facades expose `prepare`,
  `publish`, and `listen`, not `enqueue`.
- Configure TypeScript SQL outbox with generic `executor` and `transaction`
  options. Drizzle remains optional through `@qlever-llc/trellis/service/drizzle`
  adapter helpers, but do not generate direct `createSqlOutbox({ drizzle })` sugar
  or per-handler Drizzle wrapping. Trellis owns helper-table migration artifacts
  from `getSqlOutboxMigrations(...)`; services run them with their normal
  migration tool.
- NATS KV outbox/inbox helpers remain non-transactional with arbitrary SQL or
  external side effects; do not use them to claim a database write and event
  enqueue committed atomically.
- TypeScript telemetry helpers are exported from `@qlever-llc/trellis/telemetry`.
  Use `recordTrellisDuration(...)` for low-cardinality OpenTelemetry duration
  histograms and `recordTrellisError(...)` for error counters; never put user IDs,
  session keys, flow IDs, request IDs, trace IDs, contract IDs, NATS subjects, or
  URLs in metric attributes.
- Generated TypeScript SDK event aliases are event bodies. Runtime event metadata
  is available through `PreparedTrellisEvent.header` and listener context.
- Trellis signs event publishes at publish time and consumers validate event
  proofs before invoking handlers. Prepared events intentionally remain free of
  deployment or contract metadata; runtime publish adds proof headers using the
  current session.
- For live event assertions in Deno-first TypeScript integration tests, start
  `runtime.captureEvents(...)` before publishing and assert the decoded
  `{ event, payload, context, receivedAt }` records. Prefer this over raw NATS
  subscriptions or outbox-only assertions when the test must observe a published
  event through Trellis runtime authority.
- `@qlever-llc/trellis-test` exports assertion helpers including
  `assertEventCaptured`, `assertEventsCaptured`, `assertNoEventCaptured`,
  `assertNoEventDuring`, `assertJobCompleted`, `assertOperationCompleted`,
  `assertRpcOk`, `assertRpcEventuallyOk`, and `assertRpcErr` for Deno-first
  TypeScript tests. The captured-event helpers accept generated
  `runtime.captureEvents(...)` captures directly, and `assertJobCompleted`
  accepts generated service job refs directly.
- Event subject `params` must point at string, number, or integer-compatible
  payload fields. For `anyOf` or `oneOf` event payload schemas, every variant must
  contain each routed pointer.
- Feed subscriptions are connection-scoped. Closing or aborting a client feed
  propagates cancellation to the provider; watch feeds must not create a durable
  consumer per viewer.
- App and device contracts may declare schema-backed value or map State stores.
  Use generated named State facades; services use `service.kv`, and no participant
  accesses the internal `trellis_state` bucket directly. State follows the stable
  principal plus contract lineage across reconnects and compatible digest changes.

## Service repo setup

- Keep Trellis-wide AI guidance in this file or `llms-full.txt`; keep local paths,
  commands, secrets, and domain rules in the service repo's own `AGENTS.md`.
- Put TypeScript service source next to a local `deno.json`, `deno.jsonc`, or
  `package.json`. Single-contract services normally expose a top-level
  `contract.ts`; multi-contract services use `contracts/*.ts`. Contract source
  files should default-export the `define*Contract(...)` result.
- Wrap TypeScript Trellis generation in `deno task prepare`.
- In TypeScript services, run prepare/generation after contract changes before
  typing extracted handlers. Import generated SDK aliases such as
  `OrdersCreateHandler` for extracted RPC/event/feed/operation/job
  handlers. Inline `service.handle...` handlers still infer at the registration
  site.
- TypeScript handlers may return source `defineError(...)` instances when their
  serialized data matches the declared generated SDK error data; generated SDK
  aliases type those returns structurally on the handler side.
- For Deno-first TypeScript service integration tests, prefer the public
  `@qlever-llc/trellis-test/integration` helpers and
  `/integration/runner`. External service repos provide
  `trellis.integration.ts` with an explicit `runtime.trellis.command`,
  `denoTestArgs`, and case descriptors. Tests use
  `trellisIntegrationTest(...)`, `runtimeScopeForCase(CASE_ID)`, fixed authored
  contract ids/actions/subjects, case-slugged physical names/resource keys, contract approval/provisioning,
  `TrellisService.connect(...)`, and `runtime.connectClient(...)`. Serial runs
  call the runner with `--config`; shared runs add `--parallel --jobs 1`.
  Shared cases use one NATS account, Trellis process, and SQLite set; the harness
  resets stale accepted authority before attached authentication. Higher worker
  counts are rejected because fixed protocol subjects share that account. Keep
  one case per module. `trellis-test` runs NATS as a managed child process
  from pinned, checksum-verified nats-server and nsc binaries (cached under
  `TRELLIS_TEST_CACHE_DIR`, default `~/.cache/trellis-test`; first use downloads them, requiring network; every reuse revalidates the cached archive sha256 against the pin and byte-checks the cached binary against a fresh extraction, so corrupted or replaced cache entries are reinstalled, and and `sh` must be on `PATH`); no container runtime is
  required.
- The `trellis` CLI runs the runtime with
  `trellis server [mode] --config PATH [--nats URL | --nats-binary PATH]
  [--nats-state-dir PATH] [--check]` (mode defaults to `all`; `--check`
  validates configuration, trust, stores, streams, and NATS connectivity,
  then exits). Managed mode (no `--nats`) downloads the pinned nats-server
  release, verifies its checksum, caches it under `TRELLIS_CACHE_DIR`
  (default `~/.cache/trellis`), listens on 127.0.0.1 ports 4222 (NATS), 8222
  (monitoring), and 8080 (websocket), and stops the server when the CLI
  exits. `--nats URL` runs against an external server; `--nats-binary PATH`
  manages an existing trusted nats-server binary without re-verifying it;
  `--nats-state-dir PATH` keeps all mutable managed-NATS files (rendered
  configs, pid file, resolver JWTs, JetStream data) outside a read-only
  bundle.
- The runtime OCI image bakes the `trellis` CLI and the pinned,
  checksum-verified nats-server at `/usr/local/bin/nats-server`; `nsc` is
  test-harness-only and not in the image. The entrypoint stays
  `trellis-server` for external-NATS deployments. For a managed single
  container, mount the generated bundle read-only from its own named volume
  and the writable state on a second volume
  (`trellis-bundle:/etc/trellis:ro,Z`, `trellis-state:/var/lib/trellis:rw,Z`),
  with the bundle's SQLite store paths rewritten to the state volume, and run
  `trellis server ... --nats-binary /usr/local/bin/nats-server
  --nats-state-dir /var/lib/trellis/nats`.
- Test Trellis runtime behavior through live integration tests. Do not use fake
  NATS, fake Trellis runtimes, fake auth, fake generated clients, or hand-built
  bootstrap/control-plane responders to prove Trellis behavior. If a live test
  needs a missing failure or inspection surface, add the smallest named test
  helper instead of enriching a fake.
- Deployment authority plans can be `superseded`; only `pending` plans targeting
  the current desired authority version are actionable.
- Deployment authority plans expose `breakingChanges` as structured per-target
  compatibility failures for operator UI.
- Wrap Rust Trellis generation in `cargo xtask prepare`.
- Diagnose Rust generation performance with `cargo xtask prepare --timings`; the
  report includes phase and per-contract resolution times, subprocess counts,
  cache hits/misses and input validation, generation outcomes, and installed
  file/byte totals.
- Prepare caches canonical contract resolution in the platform user cache,
  repository-namespaced and disposable. Set `TRELLIS_PREPARE_CACHE` to isolate
  or relocate it; `--force` bypasses it. Declare exceptional deterministic
  resolution inputs with `trellis.prepare.inputs` globs and
  `trellis.prepare.env` names in `package.json`, or
  `[package.metadata.trellis.prepare]` in `Cargo.toml`. Undeclared time,
  randomness, network, environment, and external-file inputs are unsupported.
- Rust owner SDKs are vocabulary-only. Rust services, apps, agents, and devices
  connect only through their materialized generated participant facade. Do not
  import `trellis_rs::client` or `trellis_rs::generated` in application code.
- Browser app repos should read the Svelte AI guide before wiring
  `createTrellisApp`, `TrellisProvider`, generated service SDK aliases for
  contract `uses`, Vite aliases, or `svelte-check` path maps. Do not generate or
  import an app SDK just to type a Svelte app client; use
  `TrellisClientFor<typeof contract>` from the app source contract.
- Browser apps should let Trellis helpers own auth redirects and treat plain
  callbacks after expired login as auth-restart opportunities, not errors.
- Browser apps use Trellis browser helpers for initial auth redirects and portal
  flows. Once connected, sign-out and other auth control use generated Auth APIs
  over NATS; do not add HTTP logout, context, revocation, or client-bootstrap
  calls, hard-code IdP logout endpoints, or invent arbitrary return URLs.
- Record the local contract path, generation command, format command, typecheck
  command, test command, run command, and database migration command in the local
  `AGENTS.md`.
